anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : The optimizer relies on stale, incomplete, or missing statistics, producing cardinality misestimates that lead to systematically poor execution-plan choices.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical or virtual storage layer is saturated, so read/write latency and queue depths rise sharply, throttling database operations regardless of CPU availability.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Logical or physical free space on data, temp, or log destinations is nearly exhausted, causing allocation failures, write stalls, and related errors.

When these three conditions coincide, workloads can exhibit extreme and erratic slowdowns: queries may shift to full-table scans or spill to disk because of bad cardinality estimates, immediately overwhelming an already bandwidth-starved storage subsystem. Elevated I/O latency and deep queues amplify statement runtimes, inflating undo, redo, and temp space consumption until remaining free space collapses. Users observe escalating I/O wait times, exploding temp and log files, repeated plan re-compilations with wild estimate-to-actual divergences, sudden "out of space" or "cannot extend segment" errors, and prolonged recovery or checkpoint durations.

Causally, stale statistics can drive the optimizer to select scan-heavy or hash-intensive plans that issue far more physical reads and generate larger spills than necessary, directly aggravating storage throughput saturation. The ensuing longer execution windows and heightened write volumes accelerate space consumption in data, temp, and log areas, pushing the system toward capacity limits. As space dwindles, auto-extension failures and log-archive backpressure further inflate I/O latency, which in turn prolongs query execution and hampers automatic statistics refresh jobs, keeping statistics stale and closing a vicious feedback loop that degrades overall database performance and stability.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
